title: One failed 'Connect to Server' attempt drops the app out of Local mode permanently — every screen gets an undismissable red 'Error: not connected to server' banner and there is no way back without a restart
summary: The primary P1 (no way back short of relaunch) was already closed by an earlier wave and is proven by a revert test; two residuals the verifier reported were still open and are now fixed. Already-correct half: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/connection_settings.dart:586-588 restores the displaced local backend after a failed connect (_restoreLocalBackend at :605-616 -> BackendNotifier.useLocalBackend, packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/backend_provider.dart:249), and connection_settings.dart:140-159 adds a 'Work Locally' row (_WorkLocallyButton at :354-400) on a disconnected desktop. Residual A (fixed): packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/connection_quality_provider.dart collapsed 'not a NetworkBackend' into ConnectionQuality.local, so the Dashboard chip read a quiet grey 'Local' while the shell banner two rows above said the app was not connected — the exact contradiction the verifier logged. Added ConnectionMode.none + ConnectionQuality.disconnected and a DisconnectedBackend gate before the NetworkBackend test; the chip now renders 'No backend' in the error colour. Residual B (fixed): the two surfaces the verifier named as dead ends had no control at all. The shell banner was a bare red strip of text; it is now packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/disconnected_backend_banner.dart. The title-bar connection popover stated 'Not connected to a server' and offered nothing (it only ever rendered 'Reconnect now' / 'Disconnect', both gated on an existing NetworkBackend); packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/remote_connection_indicator.dart:522-540 now offers the same recovery, gated on `activeBackend is DisconnectedBackend` rather than on the sheet's `notConnected` status — a local FFI desktop is also 'not connected to a server', and offering it a switch to a mode it is already in would be a control that does nothing. All three surfaces — Settings > Connection, the banner and the popover — share ONE owner, new packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/work_locally.dart (switchToLocalBackend + WorkLocallyButton + canWorkLocally), so the superseded-transition case cannot be got wrong in one of three copies; the private _WorkLocallyButton in connection_settings.dart and the banner's own handler were deleted, not left alongside it. Gated to the desktop platforms whose entry point actually installs an FfiBackend (apps/desktop/lib/main.dart:178), so it is never a button to nowhere on a phone.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/connection_quality_provider_test.dart 'a DisconnectedBackend is not reported as local'; packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/dashboard/connection_quality_chip_test.dart 'a machine with no backend is not labelled Local' (drives the real provider off the real backendProvider); packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/shell/disconnected_backend_banner_test.dart — 'the shell renders the banner with its way out' pumps the REAL AppShell, plus 'the banner offers a way back and takes it' and 'the banner clears once a backend is installed'. packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/remote_connection_indicator_authority_test.dart 'with no backend the sheet offers the way back to local mode' taps the real indicator, opens the real sheet and asserts useLocalBackend ran and the backend swapped. Pre-existing cover for the primary fix: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/connection_settings_local_fallback_test.dart.
revert_check: (1) Deleted `if (backend is DisconnectedBackend) { return Stream.value(ConnectionQuality.disconnected); }` at connection_quality_provider.dart:202-204 -> core test failed 'Expected: not ConnectionMode:<ConnectionMode.local> Actual: ConnectionMode.local' and the chip test failed 'Found 1 widget with text "Local"'. (2) Deleted the `if (_canRunLocally) TextButton(...)` block in disconnected_backend_banner.dart -> 'the banner offers a way back and takes it' failed 'Found 0 widgets with text "Work Locally"'. (3) Deleted the production call site `if (!useBottomNav) const DisconnectedBackendBanner(),` in app_shell.dart -> 'the shell renders the banner with its way out' failed 'Found 0 widgets with type "DisconnectedBackendBanner"'. (4) Replaced `hadLocalBackend ? await _restoreLocalBackend() : null` in connection_settings.dart:587 with `null` -> the pre-existing 'a failed connect leaves the machine in local mode' failed (useLocalCalls Expected <1> Actual <0>). (5) Deleted the `if (activeBackend is DisconnectedBackend && canWorkLocally)` block from remote_connection_indicator.dart -> 'with no backend the sheet offers the way back to local mode' failed 'Found 0 widgets with text "Work Locally"'. All restored; suites re-run green.
caveats: backend_provider.dart:_rollbackFailedConnect still installs a fresh DisconnectedBackend on a failed connect — deliberately, per its own comment, so `backend is NetworkBackend` never reads as connected. Restoring is the caller's job because only the caller knows what it displaced. apps/desktop/lib/main.dart:249 (--remote-host client mode) still leaves the app disconnected when its explicitly requested remote target is unreachable; the banner's 'Work Locally' is now the way out there too. The 2 settings golden-capture failures in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/captures_landscape_test.dart are PRE-EXISTING, proven not assumed: with location_settings.dart and connection_settings.dart swapped back to their HEAD contents the same 2 fail with byte-identical diffs (4.38% / 17535px and 8.70% / 34883px). `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` is dirty repo-wide on this toolchain and was already dirty at HEAD for app_shell.dart, location_settings.dart and remote_connection_indicator.dart; every file I authored is format-clean and my edits add no new format delta (checked by diffing a formatted copy). The 4 dashboard golden-capture failures in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/dashboard/captures_landscape_test.dart are PRE-EXISTING (~40% pixel diff, Windows-captured goldens on Linux), proven not assumed: with connection_quality_chip.dart and connection_quality_provider.dart swapped back to their HEAD contents the same 4 fail with the same ~40% diffs. Suite evidence: skotiq_core full suite 5468 passed / 6 failed (all pre-existing nina_sequence_fidelity_test 'Wait Has No Time Set', caused by an uncommitted change to providers/sequence/rules/timing_rules.dart made before this session); skotiq_planetarium full suite 480 passed / 1 failed (benchmark golden_compare, proven pre-existing by swapping my geolocation_service.dart back to HEAD and getting byte-identical diffs). skotiq_app was run per-directory against the final source — settings 414/2, widgets+shell+dashboard 510/4, planner+planetarium 221/5, session_review+onboarding 185/2 — and EVERY failure in every one is a captures_*.dart golden-image test, the documented Windows-captured-goldens-on-Linux class. Full skotiq_app suite: 2843 passed / 45 failed. Every failure is a golden-image or screenshot test (captures_*.dart, test/golden/mosaic_project_screen_golden_test.dart, test/golden/public_screenshots_test.dart, which also times out at 10 min) — the documented Windows-captured-goldens-on-Linux class. For every directory my changes can actually reach I proved the failures pre-existing by swapping my files back to HEAD and getting identical pixel diffs. The remaining failures are in analytics / imaging / mosaic / sequencer / equipment, which import none of the code I touched: connection_quality_provider has exactly one UI consumer (the dashboard chip), horizonProfileProvider has four (settings, planner, two planetarium layouts), and work_locally / the banner / ip_geolocation / GeolocationService have no consumers outside settings, the shell and onboarding.

title: 'Use Device Location' is IP geolocation labelled as GPS, and it leaves the old elevation in place — producing a site that does not exist
summary: The three defects the finding names were already closed by an earlier wave (verified by revert): the row is 'Detect Location / Device GPS if this machine has it, otherwise a city-level estimate from your IP address' (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/location_settings.dart:258-266), a shared consent dialog gates the outbound request on BOTH surfaces (packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/geolocation_consent.dart, called from location_settings.dart:530 and packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/onboarding/steps/site_step.dart:303), and an elevation belonging to a site more than 25 km away is cleared rather than inherited (location_settings.dart:557-575, site_step.dart:326-341). The residual the VERIFIER found and nobody fixed was the transport: the request that actually ran was plain-HTTP http://ip-api.com/json/, and ip-api.com's free tier answers 403 over HTTPS, so it was cleartext by construction. Confirmed live here (`curl https://ip-api.com/json/` -> 403, `curl http://ip-api.com/json/` -> 200 with this host's real coordinates). Fixed by moving the fallback to https://ipwho.is/ (same free/no-key shape, TLS) in packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/services/geolocation_service.dart, with an injectable client so the transport itself is testable. SECOND CALL SITE, not in the finding: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/ffi_backend/sequencer_recovery_operations.dart:528 did the same thing over cleartext for the headless appliance's GET /api/location (apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/handlers/profile_handlers.dart:679). Both now route through one owner, new packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/ip_geolocation.dart, which is TLS-only AND refuses to answer a coordinate it does not have — the old parser returned 0.0 for a missing lat/lon, so a rate-limited or rewritten reply became Null Island. Also fixed a latent parse bug in both: `data['latitude'] as double?` throws on a whole-degree coordinate (JSON `40`, not `40.0`) and every caller swallowed the throw, so an observer on a round degree was told no location could be found.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/ip_geolocation_test.dart (8 tests) — asserts on the recorded request URI's SCHEME rather than a vendor name, so swapping providers later cannot reintroduce cleartext; 'the FfiBackend path uses the shared TLS lookup' and 'the FfiBackend path refuses to answer Null Island' drive the REAL FfiBackend, which is the object the headless handler calls. packages/skotiq_planetarium/test/geolocation_transport_test.dart 'every IP-geolocation request is HTTPS, including the fallback' answers the primary with ipapi.co's real rate-limited body so the FALLBACK leg — the one that was cleartext — is the leg under test.
revert_check: (1) Put `http://ip-api.com/json/` (and the old `status`/`lat`/`lon` field shape) back in geolocation_service.dart -> 'every IP-geolocation request is HTTPS, including the fallback' failed: "Expected: 'https' Actual: 'http' — http://ip-api.com/json/ left the machine in the clear". (2) Replaced `getLocationFromInternet() => IpGeolocation.fetch()` in sequencer_recovery_operations.dart with the old inline `http.get(Uri.parse('http://ip-api.com/json'))` + `?? 0.0` parser -> 'the FfiBackend path uses the shared TLS lookup' failed (recorded requests 'Expected: an object with length of <1> Actual: []' — the injected client never saw it, i.e. a real socket would have been opened) and 'the FfiBackend path refuses to answer Null Island' failed (returned a LocationSettings instead of throwing). Both restored; 8/8 and 2/2 green.
caveats: ipwho.is is a new third-party dependency for the fallback leg. It was chosen because ip-api.com cannot be used over TLS without a paid key and because the alternative — deleting the fallback — leaves detection dead whenever ipapi.co rate-limits, which the verifier proved happens from this host. The consent dialog now names it and says the request is HTTPS. getLocationFromInternet now throws instead of returning (0,0); the only production caller is the headless handler, which surfaces the error to the client — that is the intended change, and it matches the campaign's existing no-fabricated-observer-location fix. Not exercised against a live network from the app (tests use an injected client). Suite evidence: skotiq_core full suite 5468 passed / 6 failed (all pre-existing nina_sequence_fidelity_test 'Wait Has No Time Set', caused by an uncommitted change to providers/sequence/rules/timing_rules.dart made before this session); skotiq_planetarium full suite 480 passed / 1 failed (benchmark golden_compare, proven pre-existing by swapping my geolocation_service.dart back to HEAD and getting byte-identical diffs). skotiq_app was run per-directory against the final source — settings 414/2, widgets+shell+dashboard 510/4, planner+planetarium 221/5, session_review+onboarding 185/2 — and EVERY failure in every one is a captures_*.dart golden-image test, the documented Windows-captured-goldens-on-Linux class. Full skotiq_app suite: 2843 passed / 45 failed. Every failure is a golden-image or screenshot test (captures_*.dart, test/golden/mosaic_project_screen_golden_test.dart, test/golden/public_screenshots_test.dart, which also times out at 10 min) — the documented Windows-captured-goldens-on-Linux class. For every directory my changes can actually reach I proved the failures pre-existing by swapping my files back to HEAD and getting identical pixel diffs. The remaining failures are in analytics / imaging / mosaic / sequencer / equipment, which import none of the code I touched: connection_quality_provider has exactly one UI consumer (the dashboard chip), horizonProfileProvider has four (settings, planner, two planetarium layouts), and work_locally / the banner / ip_geolocation / GeolocationService have no consumers outside settings, the shell and onboarding.

title: Running an A/B recipe preview leaves a full 'Preview... 100%' progress bar pinned under the header forever, so the screen permanently claims a job is running
summary: Closed by an earlier wave and verified here by severing the production wiring. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:636-642 defines `_withLiveProgress`, a try/finally that clears `state.progress` on every exit path, and EVERY seam-driven action routes through it: integrate() :857, reIntegratePreview() :1122 (the A/B panel's 'Run both'), runColorCalibration() :1175, the shared _runFinishingStep engine used by runBackgroundExtraction/runDeconvolve/runStarReduction :1349, and runNarrowband() :1426. That is all six actions the finding's proposed_fix listed, not just reIntegratePreview. The stream binding at :651-666 still deliberately leaves a terminal 1.0 on screen (so the bar lands full) and the strip still renders for as long as progress != null (session_review_screen.dart:142-144) — the fix is the teardown, not a change to either of those.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/session_review_progress_strip_test.dart 'the preview progress strip is torn down when reIntegratePreview returns' — pumps the real SessionReviewScreen against a real controller and a seam that emits the same terminal (phase: 'preview', fraction: 1.0) the native preview integrate does (native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/post_session.rs:838), asserts on rendered widget state, and includes a control that a live 0.5 event DOES render the strip so the finder is not vacuously passing.
revert_check: Replaced `return _withLiveProgress(() async { ... });` in reIntegratePreview (session_review_controller.dart:1122) with the bare `try { ... } catch (_) { return null; }` body it wraps — i.e. the exact pre-fix shape. The test failed: 'Expected: null Actual: ({double fraction, String phase}):<(fraction: 1.0, phase: preview)>'. Restored; green.
caveats: No behaviour change was needed, so files_changed is empty by design. title: Importing a detailed .hor horizon silently collapses it to 8 sector maxima — a single tree blocks a whole 45-degree sector
summary: An earlier wave had made this a DISCLOSURE — a confirmation dialog saying 'At most 8 of the 36 survive' — on the verifier's rationale that 'the app's horizon model is 8-sector everywhere, so the reduction is intrinsic'. That rationale is wrong, and checking it is what made this fixable. Every visibility decision in the app already goes through ONE per-azimuth question, HorizonProfile.altitudeAtAzimuth: the planner's visibility filter (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planner/planner_screen_parts/_filter_controls.dart:530) and the planetarium, which builds its 360-entry terrain table from it (planetarium_shell.dart:104, planetarium_screen/layouts.dart:65 and :368). So the samples only had to survive as far as that function. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/settings_provider.dart's HorizonProfile now carries the imported samples (normalized, sorted, clamped), serialises them into the same horizon_profile_json blob AFTER the eight compass keys (so an older build still reads a valid coarse mask out of the same string), parses them back with a real jsonDecode — the hand-rolled _parseSimpleJson only ever handled flat string->number maps and would have dropped the array on every reload — and interpolates them linearly with 360-degree wrap in altitudeAtAzimuth. The eight compass fields keep their exact previous meaning as the per-sector MAXIMUM summary, so the settings page still never under-reports an obstruction. Editing any of the eight writes a samples-less blob (location_settings.dart:_updateHorizonProfile builds the 8-key JSON by hand), which is the right semantics — the operator is overriding by sector — and the page now says which of the two models is in force so the eight numbers are never mistaken for the whole story. The 29-degree tree at azimuth 190 in the finding's own repro no longer blocks azimuth 160 or 220.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/horizon_profile_import_test.dart group 'imported surveys keep their resolution' (7 tests): the file's own 36-sample repro answers 29 deg at azimuth 190 and 5 deg at 160/220, isAboveHorizon(10, 160) is true while isAboveHorizon(10, 190) is false, interpolation wraps across 360, samples survive the JSON round trip, an 8-key legacy blob still reads as the coarse smoothstep mask, a hand-edited mask carries no samples and emits no 'samples' key, a single sample stays a flat horizon, and a truncated blob still yields its compass values. packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/location_horizon_import_disclosure_test.dart (6 tests) drives the real settings page end to end: the dialog states what is kept, accepting stores all 36 samples AND answers at file resolution, and 'the page says which horizon model is in force' types into the N compass field and asserts the survey is dropped, N becomes 12, and the wording flips back to the coarse-mask sentence.
revert_check: (1) Deleted `if (_samples.length >= 2) return _interpolateSamples(az);` from altitudeAtAzimuth (settings_provider.dart:531) — the one line that makes the samples reach a decision -> 3 core tests failed, including azimuth 160 coming back 18.99 deg instead of 5 deg (the sector-maximum bleed the finding describes) and the wrap interpolation returning 0.0. (2) Deleted `samples: samples` from HorizonProfile.fromSamples so the import parses but does not retain -> 2 app tests failed: 'Expected: <36> Actual: <0>' for the stored sample count, and 'Found 0 widgets with text containing An imported survey of 36'. Both restored; 16/16 core and 6/6 app green, plus location_horizon_import_authority_test.dart and location_settings_truth_test.dart (20 total) green.
caveats: The blob grows (a 360-sample 1-degree survey serialises to roughly 5 KB of JSON in the app_settings TEXT column). horizon_profile_json remains deliberately non-remotable (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/settings_sections/app_settings_partial_persistence_mapping.dart:27), so this does not go on the wire; the scalar effective_horizon_deg floor is unchanged. The separate samples-based scheduler HorizonProfile (services/scheduler/horizon_profile.dart, the horizon_profiles table attached to TargetSchedulerNode) is a different feature and was not touched. _interpolateSamples binary-searches rather than scanning, because the planetarium rebuilds a 360-entry terrain table from altitudeAtAzimuth on every sky-view build and a 1-degree survey would otherwise cost ~65k comparisons per frame. Not exercised in a running GUI, only in widget tests. The 5 planner golden-capture failures in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/planner/captures_*.dart are PRE-EXISTING, proven not assumed: with the two load-bearing lines of this fix removed the same 5 fail with byte-identical pixel diffs (7.63% / 6.97% / 13.39%). Full skotiq_app suite: 2843 passed / 45 failed. Every failure is a golden-image or screenshot test (captures_*.dart, test/golden/mosaic_project_screen_golden_test.dart, test/golden/public_screenshots_test.dart, which also times out at 10 min) — the documented Windows-captured-goldens-on-Linux class.
